claim_checks.evidence: Official INCI (59 ingredients) lists every ingredient in the draft: Niacinamide #3, Hydroxypinacolone Retinoate #17, Bisabolol #25, Retinyl Palmitate #30, Ceramide NP #44, Ceramide AP #50, Phytosphingosine #51, Cholesterol #52, Acetyl Hexapeptide-1 #56 (exact peptide name confirmed as 'Acetyl Hexapeptide-1'), Ceramide EOP #59, plus 13 hyaluronic-acid forms (Potassium Hyaluronate, Sodium Hyaluronate, Hyaluronic Acid, Sodium Acetylated Hyaluronate, Hydrolyzed Hyaluronic Acid, Hydroxypropyltrimonium Hyaluronate, Sodium Hyaluronate Crosspolymer, Sodium Sulfated Hyaluronate, Dimethylsilanol Hyaluronate, Hydrolyzed Sodium Hyaluronate, Hydrolyzed Calcium Hyaluronate, Sodium Stearoyl Hyaluronate, Sodium Oleoyl Hyaluronate). No Parfum/Fragrance in the list, so the official fragrance-free statement ('ปราศจาก พาราเบน, มิเนอรัล ออยล์, สารแต่สี, น้ำหอม') is consistent with the INCI. Caveat not in the draft: the formula lists 'Alcohol' (ethanol) at #23 and BHT at #22. Cross-checked against Watsons Thailand (BP_316344), beautybuddy.co and Skinsort - all identical.

Official INCI (36 ingredients) contains all ten: Niacinamide #2, Tranexamic Acid #16, Allantoin #18, Alpha-Arbutin #22, Fragrance(Parfum) #25, Glycolic Acid #26, Sodium Ascorbyl Phosphate #29, Ascorbic Acid #30, Ascorbyl Glucoside #31, Tocopherol #35. So Ascorbic Acid and Glycolic Acid ARE genuinely in the INCI even though the official marketing copy does not mention them. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: Glycolic Acid sits at #26 of 36, immediately AFTER the fragrance - this indicates a very low level (consistent with a pH-adjuster / minor role, not an exfoliating dose) and it should not be described as an AHA exfoliant for this serum. The three vitamin C forms (#29-31) are likewise listed after the fragrance. Identical list on INCIDecoder (uploaded 2022-12-24) and live Watsons Thailand (BP_300660).

Each of the five ingredients occurs somewhere in the Skin Moisture Burst line, but NO single product contains all five, so the claim is wrong as a line-wide statement. Per product - Essence: niacinamide #6, panthenol #8, sodium hyaluronate #18; NO trehalose, NO centella. Serum: niacinamide #3, sodium hyaluronate #22; NO panthenol, NO trehalose, NO centella. Gel Cream: trehalose #9, sodium hyaluronate #16, centella (extract #18, leaf extract #21, plus madecassoside, asiaticoside); NO niacinamide, NO panthenol. 15X Ampoule Mask: niacinamide #5, trehalose #18, sodium hyaluronate #30; NO panthenol, NO centella. Bi-Phase Cleansing Water: niacinamide #10, sodium hyaluronate; NO panthenol, trehalose or centella. The only functional 'hero' ingredients common to all five products are Glyceryl Glucoside and Sodium Hyaluronate (the rest of the shared set is base/preservative-system material: Water, Glycerin, Butylene Glycol, 1,2-Hexanediol, Ethylhexylglycerin, Disodium EDTA). The official serum-page hero list is confirmed: Glyceryl Glucoside #9, Betaine #5, Witch Hazel Extract #21, and 'hyaluronic acid' present as Sodium Hyaluronate #22.

Confirmed for all three leave-on Barrier Boost products - Essence: Panthenol #7, Dipotassium Glycyrrhizate #11, Ectoin #15. Serum: Panthenol #7, Dipotassium Glycyrrhizate #12, Ectoin #18. Soothing Gel Cream: Panthenol #9, Dipotassium Glycyrrhizate #13, Ectoin #21. NOT true for the Cleansing Gel Foam, which contains Ectoin (#24) only - no panthenol and no dipotassium glycyrrhizate - and additionally contains Parfum (Fragrance) #15 and two colourants. The actives genuinely shared by all four Barrier Boost products are Ectoin, Centella Asiatica Leaf Extract and Centella Asiatica Leaf Vesicles (marketed as 'Cicazome').
